articles.title: Mass Effect Fans Call for EA Boycott as Petition to Save BioWare's Canceled Game Garners More than 75,000 Signatures
articles.summary: Mass Effect fans are calling for a boycott of all EA products and services in protest of the company closing down BioWare and canceling the next Mass Effect game. It’s a rough time for Mass Effect fans.
body: It’s a rough time for Mass Effect fans. On October 21, EA announced its plans to shut down BioWare, a 30-year-old studio that spearheaded RPGs in the West with titles like Dragon Age, Jade Empire, Baldur’s Gate, and of course, Mass Effect.
Players were eagerly awaiting news of the next game in BioWare’s beloved sci-fi franchise — but EA shut that down, too, revealing in a statement that the project was officially canceled.

In the two days since then, fans of BioWare and the Mass Effect series have gathered together to call for action, begging EA to at least sell off BioWare’s IP to other studios rather than letting them languish. In fact, tensions have become so strained that players are now calling for an outright boycott of EA’s products and services until something is done.
On Reddit, several threads are rallying Mass Effect fans to gather under the hashtag #savemasseffect, urging players to take action and make their voices heard.

articles.title: Call Of Duty: Modern Warfare 4’s First DLC Is Out Now, Honors A Real Soldier Who Sustained Gruesome Injuries
articles.summary: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 released today, October 23, and the game's first DLC pack is available now. In keeping with Call of Duty tradition, the day-one DLC is a Call of Duty Endowment (CODE) pack, with proceeds going to Activision's charity that supports military veterans find new jobs after…
body: The CODE Valor Pack adds the real-life Medal of Honor recipient Kyle Carpenter to the game as a playable character.

Carpenter was in Marjah, Afghanistan, when, on November 21, 2010, he put himself in front of a grenade to help save the life of his fellow Marine, Nick Eufrazio. Carpenter sustained serious injuries from the grenade blast. He was unconscious for five weeks, had his teeth stripped from his mouth, and lost an eye. He sustained numerous other life-threatening injuries in the blast.

Carpenter underwent brain surgery to remove shrapnel from his head. He had about 40 other surgeries to addresses his injuries, which included a collapsed lung, fractured fingers, and one arm that broke in more than 30 places. He had multiple skin grafts and now has a prosthetic eye, a new jaw, and new teeth.

The Valor Pack includes the Relentless and Valor skins, along with new weapon blueprints, a combat knife, and a weapon charm, among other things. All proceeds from the $20 DLC bundles will go to the CODE charity.

articles.title: This Massive 70" 4K Fire TV Drops to a Mere $299.99 With Free Delivery Ahead of Black Friday
articles.summary: Ahead of Black Friday, Best Buy is offering the lowest price I've seen this year for a massive (70" or higher) TV. For this week only, you can pick up the 70" Insignia F50 4K Fire TV for just $299.99 with free shipping.
body: As far as TVs are concerned, my rule of thumb is bigger is better as long as you have enough space. If you're on a budget and want the best bang for your buck, screen size will nearly always make a bigger impression than any other feature. The Insignia F50 is a void-filling 70" TV featuring a native 4K 60Hz display with HDR10 and HLG support and built-in Fire TV.

This is a solid TV for PlayStation 5 gaming despite the fact that it doesn't have a native 120Hz refresh rate. Unless you're rocking a PS5 Pro, the vast majority of games can't push past 60fps. Playing Grand Theft Auto 6 on a 70" TV, for example, will be a much more profound real-world experience than playing it on a 120Hz TV. Likewise, the Insignia F50 is a great TV for Nintendo Switch gamers because the Switch 2 only supports 60Hz at 4K in docked mode.
For the amount you save compared to getting a higher end TV, you could buy yourself a ton of video games and maybe even another console. For many (probably most) people, that's money better spent.

articles.summary: Prolific and veteran gaming actor Jennifer Hale, who is known for voicing Commander Shepard in the Mass Effect series, has reacted to the closure of BioWare and the cancellation of the next game in the series.
body: She added: "I’m holding hope for magic to happen. This community and you incredible vevs deserve that and more."

A "Save Mass Effect" Change.org petition was launched this week to urge EA to "take decisive action by committing to the continued development of Mass Effect." The petition has more than 65,000 signatures so far.

All of BioWare's new releases in the past decade--Mass Effect: Andromeda, Anthem, and Dragon Age: The Veilguard--were commercial disappointments. Against that backdrop, closing the studio makes a lot of financial sense, but it's upsetting to the millions of Mass Effect fans who adore the franchise and want to see it continue.
Based on insider reporting, the new Mass Effect game would have mixed covert ops with John Wick-inspired action, and that got a lot of people excited about what could have been.

Dantics says that Mass Effect Universe was set over 600 years after the Reaper War, and players would step into the boots of a customizable N7 agent. articles.title: 7 Classic JRPGs That Are So Good They Never Need a Remake
articles.summary: Remakes, remasters, and reimaginings are all the rage right now in video games. For the last several years, studios the world over have crafted new and vastly improved versions of all-time classic games, ranging from faithful modernizations like Capcom’s Resident Evil 4 remake to Square Enix’s…
body: Here are seven JRPGs that have aged like fine wine. These games may have been ported to newer platforms or lightly remastered at various points, but they look and play nearly identical to when they were first released.

In the waning days of the PlayStation 1 era, Square turned its back on the steampunk grit of Final Fantasy 7 and 8 and did something totally unexpected by taking the series back to good, old-fashioned medieval fantasy. With a chipper hero accompanied by a sassy princess who yearns to escape the strictures of royal life, FF9 is a heartfelt examination of love, life, and mortality that’s also a love letter to the genre. Rumors of a remake have been churning around this one for years, but last year’s 25th anniversary came and went without an announcement. And honestly, FF9 doesn’t need a remake. The visuals and music were stunning back in 2000 and still hold up brilliantly today.
A weekly cheat sheet to what you’ll eventually love to play. No buying, no commitment — just saving for later.

articles.title: Every Marvel Post-Credits Scene That Went Nowhere (So Far)
articles.summary: Once the Infinity Saga wrapped with 2019’s Spider-Man: Far From Home, Marvel had to find a new central organizing factor, a way to give all the crossovers, cataclysmic conflicts, and multiverse mayhem some meaning.
body: Over the past 18 years, Marvel Studios has focused as much on the continuity of its ongoing mega-story as it’s focused on the content of any given superhero film. The 23-film Infinity Saga was never just about individual movie narratives — it was about the buildup to Avengers: Infinity War and Avengers: Endgame, the two-part blockbuster event that brought the entire sprawling Marvel Cinematic Universe together for one grand battle royale.

So in case you ever find yourself wondering, Hey, whatever happened to Charlize Theron's character in that one Doctor Strange flick? or Wait, Harry Styles was in a Marvel movie?, here’s a helpful rundown of all the cliffhangers and post-credits sequences that Marvel hasn’t fully paid off yet.

In a mid-credits scene, Wong summons Shang-Chi/Shaun (Simu Liu) and Katy (Awkwafina) to Kamar-Taj. There, they meet Bruce Banner and Carol Danvers — who teleconference in as holograms — to discuss the origins of Shang-Chi’s superpowered rings. The rings, our Avengers pals say, are an ancient beacon transmitting an unknown message to an unknown recipient.

articles.title: WoW: Forever’s Divisive Layering Will See Major Improvements For Launch, Blizzard Says
articles.summary: World of Warcraft: Forever's layering system will receive some significant improvements for launch, according to a statement provided to GameSpot from Blizzard. Layering, for the uninitiated, is a behind-the-scenes system in WoW: Forever that essentially creates and runs new versions (or layers) of…
body: There are some pros to this system. It makes completing quests easier (since there's less competition for quests items and enemies) and the world far less crowded. It also helps performance, as anytime there are thousands of players in a concentrated area, like a capital city, the game can struggle to handle the load. Layering spreads those players out. It works wonders in modern WoW and has also been used to different degrees in various versions of WoW Classic in the past.

Unfortunately, there are also some huge downsides that have repeatedly surfaced over the course of the WoW: Forever beta. It doesn't take much searching on YouTube or Reddit to find countless instances of players complaining about layering. Leaving a group, crossing into a different zone, or traveling on a zeppelin or boat causes players to abruptly switch layers. The layering changes feel far more frequent and noticeable than in the past, ruining some of the charm that comes from having a persistent world filled with the same people.

articles.title: An '80s Cult Horror-Comedy Becomes a Global Streaming Hit on HBO Max
articles.summary: There was a time when horror movies weren't afraid to get a little weird. The 1980s gave us everything from the surreal nightmares of A Nightmare on Elm Street to the gooey, creature-filled chaos of The Blob.
body: There's one 80s classic that perfectly toed the horror-comedy line — it's part Christmas fantasy, part creature-feature nightmare, and part pitch-black comedy. It's the kind of movie that can make you laugh one minute and recoil in disgust the next, and it's trending right now on streaming.

Gremlins, Joe Dante's 1984 horror comedy, remains a masterclass in balancing laughs with genuine scares. More than four decades later, its mischievous monsters are still just as entertaining, and the film is finding an audience on HBO Max. It's ranked third on the platform's top movies chart, according to FlixPatrol.

Gremlins follows Billy Peltzer (Zach Galligan), a young man who receives an unusual Christmas present from his father: a small, furry creature called a Mogwai. Billy names his new pet Gizmo, but caring for the adorable little creature comes with three important rules: keep it away from bright light, never let it touch water, and never feed it after midnight.

articles.title: Nintendo's Shigeru Miyamoto says even if gen-AI "were to eventually handle everything, there will always be a role left" for human designers
articles.summary: Legendary Nintendo developer Shigeru Miyamoto - who led development on classic games such as Super Mario 64 and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time - has argued that the rise of generative AI tools won't necessarily replace human talent.
body: Next month, Shigeru Miyamoto will become the first ever video game developer to be awarded the Order of Culture by the Emperor of Japan, a hugely prestigious honour. But in a recent press conference dedicated to the award, he also shared some thoughts about gen-AI and its use in game production.

"Our generation lived through a period of rapid computer development - a time when tools were constantly evolving, moving from typewriters to word processors,” he said while speaking to the press, in quotes translated by VGC. Miyamoto argued that a designer's true capabilities "finally came to the fore" as technology advanced and was capable of handling more of what might be considered "labor", and a similar transition may take place with generative AI tech.

"While the act of creation is inherently satisfying, there's a danger: one might find satisfaction in the labor itself and mistakenly believe that a high-quality piece of work has been created," he added. If generative-AI software replaces more tasks involved in game production, human game devs might have "an opportunity to reflect on what's really important."

articles.title: With Minecraft and Diablo shows already on the way, Netflix reportedly offered Xbox $500m for a bigger film and TV deal
articles.summary: A deal between Netflix and Xbox has supposedly fallen through because of one minor quibble: Netflix wanted to adapt the console maker's games for $500m, not $800m.
body: That's according to Puck News ' Matt Belloni, who reports that Netflix offered Xbox $500m to exclusively licence the company's games and turn them into streamable films or TV shows for the next seven years.

Xbox CEO Asha Sharma and the division's business affairs team then responded with an eye-watering counter offer, according to the report. Xbox supposedly asked the streamer for $800m to sign off on the same deal.

Former Netflix CCO Bela Bajaria reportedly approached the game publisher first, but the executive's departure and Xbox's expensive counter offer led to the deal falling apart. Netflix CFO Spence Neumann was apparently one of the streamer's top heads who thought the deal wasn't worth the $800m price tag.

It's unclear which games would've been included in the film and TV deal considering multiple Xbox brands are already on their way to screens both big and small. Amazon is working to adapt Wolfenstein into a live-action series and will soon debut the third season of its acclaimed Fallout show, for example, while Paramount is turning Call of Duty into a blockbuster movie.
points: A deal between Netflix and Xbox has supposedly fallen through because of one minor quibble: Netflix wanted to adapt the console maker's games for $500m, not $800m.

articles.title: Based on player data, Capcom's pretty happy with the difficulty level of Onimusha: Way of the Sword: 'We think it's hit the right spot'
articles.summary: One of the big topics of conversation around Onimusha: Way of the Sword when it released last month—and even before that, when Capcom first put out a demo of the game—was whether it was too easy.
body: Way of the Sword's harder difficulty option being locked behind beating the campaign didn't necessarily endear the game to hardcore action players, either, so I'm not shocked that one of the most popular downloads on the game's Nexusmods page is one that amps up enemy aggression.

But I still mostly loved Onimusha, and didn't find myself craving the brutal difficulty of Sekiro or Nioh while I was playing it. With more than a month of hindsight to see how players have studied the blade, Capcom also seems pretty happy with the level of challenge it settled on.

"We've been looking at the data that comes back from people playing, so we can see where people are struggling and how they're progressing through the game. What we've seen in the trends in the data is that it's close to what we set out to achieve, in terms of difficulty," director Satoru Nihei said in an interview with PC Gamer.
Nihei elaborated that Capcom has observed players being able to progress through the story, but not entirely without friction.

videos.summary: Don't miss the Gameplay Trailer for Crossout Remastered, a vehicular post-apocalyptic MMO developed by Targem Games. Players will duke it out on the battlefield with vehicles of destruction to traverse dangerous lands and soar through the skies.
points: Don't miss the Gameplay Trailer for Crossout Remastered, a vehicular post-apocalyptic MMO developed by Targem Games.
Players will duke it out on the battlefield with vehicles of destruction to traverse dangerous lands and soar through the skies.
Craft new parts, make use of lethal weapons, and survive the onslaught to attain victory.
Crossout Remastered is available now for PlayStation 4 (PS4), PlayStation 5 (PS5), Xbox One, Xbox Series X|S, and PC (Steam).

videos.title: Phantom Blade Zero - Launch Trailer | PS5 Games
videos.summary: Phantom Blade Zero launches October 29. Pre-load begins October 27. The physical edition arrives in 2027.
body: Play as Soul and cut through a conspiracy that threatens the Wulin. Experience a tale of love, loyalty, and vengeance among dear friends and old comrades. Fight for those whose last hope rests with you, and uncover the secret carried in your own blood.

videos.title: ARC Raiders - Official Soul's Offering Teaser Trailer
videos.summary: Check out the latest teaser trailer for ARC Raiders for the third-person extraction shooter game for a peek at the upcoming Soul's Offering Raider Project. The Soul's Offering Raider Project begins October 27, 2026.
body: From the trailer's official description: "It's time to honor Toledo's fallen. Light up the night sky and offer remembrances for the Raiders that came before."

videos.title: Carry The Glass - Launch Trailer | PS5 Games
videos.summary: Team up as two quirky construction workers in this fun 2-player co-op platformer! Carry a fragile glass window through colorful levels filled with challenges. Communicate and coordinate to dodge obstacles and solve puzzles. Can you finish the job without breaking the glass?
